paragraphs.en: The weather in Texas may have cooled since the recent extreme heat, but the temperature will be high at the State Board of Education meeting in Austin this month as officials debate how climate change is taught in Texas schools.
paragraphs.zh: 自最近的极端高温之后，得克萨斯州的天气可能已经转凉，但本月在奥斯汀举行的州教育委员会会议上，气氛将会十分火热，因为官员们将就得州学校应如何教授气候变化展开辩论。

paragraphs.en: Pat Hardy, who sympathises with the views of the energy sector, is resisting proposed changes to science standards for pre-teen pupils. These would emphasise the primacy of human activity in recent climate change and encourage discussion of mitigation measures.
paragraphs.zh: 帕特·哈迪认同能源行业的观点，正在抵制对未满13岁学生的科学课程标准所提出的修改建议。这些修改将强调人类活动在近期气候变化中的首要作用，并鼓励讨论减缓气候变化的措施。

paragraphs.en: Most scientists and experts sharply dispute Hardy's views. "They casually dismiss the career work of scholars and scientists as just another misguided opinion. " says Dan Quinn, senior communications strategist at the Texas Freedom Network, a non-profit group that monitors public education. "What millions of Texas kids learn in their public schools is determined too often by the political ideology of partisan board members, rather than facts and sound scholarship. "
paragraphs.zh: 大多数科学家和专家强烈反对哈迪的观点。“他们随随便便就把学者和科学家毕生的研究工作，斥为又一种误入歧途的意见，”监督公共教育的非营利组织“得州自由网络”的高级传播策略师丹·奎因说，“数百万得州孩子在公立学校学到什么，太多时候取决于带有党派倾向的委员会成员的政治意识形态，而不是事实和可靠的学术研究。”

paragraphs.en: Such debates reflect fierce discussions across the US and around the world, as researchers, policymakers, teachers and students step up demands for a greater focus on teaching about the facts of climate change in schools.
paragraphs.zh: 这样的辩论反映了美国各地乃至全世界正在展开的激烈讨论：研究人员、政策制定者、教师和学生正越来越强烈地要求，学校更加重视教授有关气候变化的事实。

paragraphs.en: A study last year by the National Center for Science Education, a non-profit group of scientists and teachers, looking at how state public schools across the country address climate change in science classes, gave barely half of US states a grade B+ or higher. Among the 10 worst performers were some of the most populous states, including Texas, which was given the lowest grade (F) and has a disproportionate influence because its textbooks are widely sold elsewhere.
paragraphs.zh: 由科学家和教师组成的非营利组织“美国国家科学教育中心”去年开展了一项研究，考察全美各州公立学校如何在科学课堂上讲授气候变化，结果只有勉强一半的州获得了B+或更高的评分。在表现最差的10个州中，有一些是人口最多的州，包括得克萨斯州。得州得到最低评分F，而且由于该州的教材在其他地方广泛销售，它的影响力远超自身范围。

paragraphs.en: Glenn Branch, the centre's deputy director, cautions that setting state-level science standards is only one limited benchmark in a country that decentralises decisions to local school boards. Even if a state is considered a high performer in its science standards, "that does not mean it will be taught", he says.
paragraphs.zh: 该中心副主任格伦·布兰奇提醒说，在这样一个将决策权下放给地方学区教育委员会的国家，制定州一级科学课程标准，只能作为一个有限的衡量指标。他说，即使某个州的科学课程标准被认为表现出色，“也不意味着这些内容一定会被教授”。

paragraphs.en: Another issue is that, while climate change is well integrated into some subjects and at some ages—such as earth and space sciences in high schools—it is not as well represented in curricula for younger children and in subjects that are more widely taught, such as biology and chemistry. It is also less prominent in many social studies courses.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个问题是，虽然气候变化已很好地融入某些学科和某些年龄段的教学，例如高中的地球与空间科学，但它在低龄儿童的课程以及生物、化学等开设更广泛的学科中，体现得还不够充分。在许多社会研究课程中，这一主题也不够突出。

paragraphs.en: Branch points out that, even if a growing number of official guidelines and textbooks reflect scientific consensus on climate change, unofficial educational materials that convey more slanted perspectives are being distributed to teachers. They include materials sponsored by libertarian think-tanks and energy industry associations.
paragraphs.zh: 布兰奇指出，即使越来越多的官方教学指南和教科书反映了有关气候变化的科学共识，一些传达更有偏向性观点的非官方教学材料仍在发放给教师。这些材料中包括由自由意志主义智库以及能源行业协会资助的资料。
